title: Variant Harmonization: Compatibility Matrix Refresh & Tooling Onboarding
creator: Maya Patel
description: Refresh the canonical compatibility matrix that drives smart routing fallbacks. Ensure tokenizer, sequence-length context, KV cache semantics, and ops/tooling hooks are harmonized across primary and fallback variant families. Create onboarding scripts and a validator to keep the matrix up-to-date as new model builds and optimizations land.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical matrix updated and checked into infra repo; versioned metadata for all active variant families
Automated validator detects tokenizer mismatches and KV cache shape incompatibilities with clear failure messages
Onboarding script can register a new model variant and produce a compatibility report in under 15 minutes
Routing tests exercise at least three realistic tier-routing scenarios across two regions using fallback chains that transit through compatible variants
Telemetry emits a compatibility_status metric and the console dashboard surfaces incompatible fallbacks with suggested mitigations
tasks: Inventory current variant families and extract tokenizer/tokenizer-config hashes
Design a lightweight compatibility schema (fields: tokenizer_hash, max_context_tokens, kv_shape_signature, required_tooling_hooks)
Implement a validator service that compares a variant's runtime artifact against schema and produces human-readable diffs
Wire compatibility_status into smart-routing decision path (soft fail mode first, then hard enforcement after 2 cycles)
Create integration test harness to simulate tier routing and region failover using local variants and recorded traces
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Routing, and Console teams; scoped the validator contract
2025-02-24: Prototype schema committed to github.com/redwood/compat-schema PR#312; initial tokenizer_hash extraction script complete
2025-02-28: Validator PoC runs against three internal variants; surfaced two KV-shape mismatches and one tooling hook mismatch
2025-03-03: Onboarding CLI skeleton merged to infra-tools; added CI job that runs validator on every variant publish
2025-03-05: Telemetry event "compatibility_status" defined; Console engineering confirmed dashboard slot for incompatibility alerts
decisions: Use SHA256 of tokenizer.json + vocab binary as tokenizer_hash instead of full tokenizer blob to keep storage small
Represent KV cache 'shape' as a short signature (num_heads|head_dim|kv_dtype) to capture the common incompatibility surface
Start with soft enforcement in routing (log + metric + suggested fallback) for 2 release cycles before flipping to reject-incompatible-fallbacks
Make validator results human-readable diffs to aid on-call remediation rather than opaque pass/fail codes
comments: Liam O'Connor (2025-02-21): Validator should emit the raw tokenizer_hash in logs to speed triage
Nora Singh (2025-02-25): Please include a short-runbook for remediation when KV-shape mismatches are reported
Ava Chen (2025-03-02): Integration tests passed for eu-west-1 -> us-central-1 failover scenario; found subtle whitespace tokenization diff with legacy-v2 variant
Diego Ramos (2025-03-04): Moving to soft enforcement flag gated by runtime-feature 'compat_enforce_v1'
risks: Tokenization diffs can be caused by upstream tokenizers that normalize whitespace differently; this may generate noisy incompatibility alerts
Automated gating too aggressive could cause unexpected routing rejections affecting customer SLAs
Incomplete variant metadata at publish time could allow incompatible variants into fallback chains
mitigations: Provide a tolerant comparison mode that highlights likely-noise diffs and a strict mode that enforces exact parity
Roll out soft enforcement first and monitor compatibility_status metrics for two cycles before hard enforcement
Add CI gating at variant-publish to require metadata fields and run validator, failing the publish if metadata is missing
